projects.name: Onboarding Drop-off Analysis
projects.objective: Understand why new customers abandon the onboarding process before completing setup.
projects.customerSegment: New signups in the last 30 days
projects.businessContext: Trial-to-paid conversion fell from 18% to 11% after the Q3 onboarding redesign.
projects.desiredOutcome: Identify the primary onboarding friction points and determine if verification or team invite is causing drop-offs.

brief.primaryQuestion: Why do new signups abandon the onboarding process before completing workspace setup?
subQuestions: At which step of onboarding do most drop-offs occur according to feedback?
What technical or usability roadblocks are users encountering during email verification?
Do enterprise users drop off for different reasons than solo practitioners?
brief.targetSegment: New signups in the last 30 days
limitationsAndAmbiguities: Support tickets over-represent vocal users encountering bugs and under-represent passive abandoners who simply leave silently.
clarificationQuestions: Are drop-offs measured at first login or at team invitation completion?
brief.recommendedFocus: Focus on separating technical verification hurdles from product complexity during setup.

sources.exclusionNotes: 1 blank feedback record excluded from calculations.

analysis.exclusionsReason: 1 empty comment row without feedback was excluded from metric calculations.

recurringThemes.name: Email Verification Delay & Spam Filtering
recurringThemes.description: Users report waiting 10-15 minutes for 6-digit confirmation codes or finding them buried in corporate spam folders.

representativeQuotes.quote: I waited 20 minutes for the verification code email. By the time it arrived, I had moved on to test another tool.
Corporate firewall blocked the no-reply code email. Need an option to use Google SSO instead of forced email code.

recurringThemes.potentialCauses: SendGrid deliverability throttling on new domain and lack of Google SSO fallback during signup.

recurringThemes.name: Forced Team Member Invitation Screen
recurringThemes.description: Step 3 requires inviting at least two colleagues before reaching the workspace, frustrating solo users and evaluators.

representativeQuotes.quote: I just wanted to test the product myself before introducing it to my team, but the UI blocked me until I typed 2 email addresses.
The Skip Invite button is almost invisible gray text on white. Thought it was mandatory.

recurringThemes.potentialCauses: Growth experiment forcing viral invitations prematurely.

painPoints.problem: Verification code latency causes users to abandon before ever seeing the workspace dashboard.
painPoints.circumstances: Occurs during initial email signup, especially on Outlook and corporate Microsoft 365 inboxes.
painPoints.implications: High initial acquisition cost wasted; estimated 30%+ drop before account activation.

supportingEvidence.quote: Code took 14 minutes. The token expired upon clicking.

painPoints.problem: Compulsory team invite step halts solo evaluators.
painPoints.implications: Creates unnecessary friction for the champion evaluating the tool on behalf of their company.

supportingEvidence.quote: Blocked me until I typed 2 email addresses.

sentiment.summary: Predominantly frustrated tone focused on onboarding gating mechanisms and slow verification.

outliers.observation: One enterprise IT manager praised the strict domain-matching security rule despite user complaints.
outliers.minorityPerspective: Security compliance administrators value mandatory verification codes even if end users experience friction.
outliers.evidence: Glad you require domain verification upfront, helps prevent unauthorized employee signups.

keyInsights.title: Verification latency is the most acute technical friction in the uploaded tickets
keyInsights.explanation: 52% of uploaded negative tickets explicitly cite waiting more than 10 minutes for email tokens or code expiration.

supportingQuotes.quote: Waited 20 minutes for the verification code email. Moved on to another tool.

keyInsights.limitations: Support tickets inherently capture users who bothered to write support; passive abandoners who left without submitting a ticket are not recorded here.

sufficiencyAssessment.statusHeadline: Partially Sufficient Evidence — Key Root Causes Identified, But Silent Abandonment Rate Unknown
whatDataEstablishes: Customers who reach out to support are heavily impacted by email verification delays and forced team invites.
The Skip button on Step 3 suffers from low contrast and confusing microcopy.
whatRemainsUnknown: What percentage of users who drop off do so because of verification delays vs lack of feature interest or pricing concerns?
Do users who drop off without contacting support encounter the same issues, or do they abandon due to unfulfilled value expectations?
sufficiencyAssessment.whyEvidenceCannotAnswer: Support tickets represent vocal complainants (approx 2-5% of total signups). They cannot measure the silent majority who abandoned without filing a ticket.
sufficiencyAssessment.recommendedMethodTitle: Targeted Pulse Survey to Abandoned Signups
sufficiencyAssessment.rationale: A lightweight 3-question survey sent to users who dropped off 24-48 hours ago will quantify whether email delays or value propositions caused their departure.
sufficiencyAssessment.suggestedSurveyFocus: Exit reasons, verification experience, and missing setup expectations.

recommendations.title: Make Team Member Invites Optional with High-Contrast "Skip for Now" Action
recommendations.problemAddressed: Solo evaluators and champions are blocked from testing the product independently.
recommendations.evidenceSupporting: 8 out of 27 tickets specifically complained about being forced to invite colleagues before seeing product value.
recommendations.expectedOutcomeHypothesis: Increasing the visibility of "Skip for now" will eliminate immediate bounce on Step 3 for solo evaluators.
recommendations.priorityRationale: Low engineering effort, immediate reduction in onboarding gatekeeper friction.
recommendations.suggestedNextStep: Redesign Step 3 CTA button to provide prominent primary "Skip for now and explore solo" link.

recommendations.title: Enable One-Click Google and Microsoft SSO on Initial Signup
recommendations.problemAddressed: Verification code emails are throttled by spam filters or delivered with 10-15 minute latency.
recommendations.evidenceSupporting: 14 tickets cited waiting for email codes or corporate firewall blocks.
recommendations.expectedOutcomeHypothesis: OAuth SSO bypasses email delivery latency entirely for over 60% of corporate users.
recommendations.priorityRationale: Directly addresses the largest volume of support tickets.
recommendations.suggestedNextStep: Implement Google & Microsoft OAuth on signup modal.

surveys.title: CloudDesk Onboarding Experience Check-in
surveys.introduction: We noticed you started setting up CloudDesk recently. Help us understand what got in your way with 3 quick questions (less than 1 minute).

questions.text: What was the main reason you paused your setup?
options: Was asked to invite team members too early
Could not find the feature I needed
Ran out of time / will finish later
questions.addressesResearchGap: Quantifies whether verification latency or forced invites causes the largest silent drop-off.

questions.text: How smooth was the initial account verification?
questions.addressesResearchGap: Measures verification friction score across non-support respondents.

questions.text: What is one thing we could change to make setup easier for you?

surveys.closingMessage: Thank you for your feedback! Your input directly helps us simplify onboarding.

answers.q3: Allow logging in with Google directly so I do not have to check spam folders.

answers.q1: Was asked to invite team members too early
answers.q3: Let me play with demo data before asking me to invite my team manager.
